messages:
alex: Heads-up — prod inference pods started failing to pull model-artifacts via our interface endpoint that routes egress through the on-prem proxy. Seeing a bunch of 504s from the loader. Anyone else?
ryan: same, image pull backoff in cluster-a around 08:14 UTC. ecr pulls also affected.
maria: quick sanity check — can someone curl the registry from a jump in that subnet and paste output?
alex: pasted from a pod node (shortened):
```
$ curl -v https://models-registry.internal
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to 10.12.34.56 (10.12.34.56) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1\n> Host: models-registry.internal\n\n* Received HTTP/0.0 when not allowed\n* Empty reply from server
```
ryan: tcpdump from node shows SYN -> SYN leaves towards tgw, never see SYN-ACK back on the node. traceroute stops at the TGW transit hop.
lisa: what routes are on the subnet? That TGW path looks suspicious. Are endpoint ENIs in the same AZ/subnet? If replies are routed to on-prem and come back via TGW they might get SNATed and SGs on the vpce ENI could drop them.
tam: checked the VPCE SG — it only allows inbound 443 from our VPC CIDR (10.12.0.0/16). On-prem proxy translates source to 172.30.0.5 when it forwards, so reply src doesn't match SG. Could be asymmetric path + SG mismatch.
ops-bot: deploy: rolling restart started for inference-loader (canary) — user: infra-automation.
maria: can you confirm whether source/dest check is enabled on the ENI? VPCE ENIs are normal ENIs with owner `vpce-` and SD-check should be true by default. If TGW is involved we need routes that return directly or SGs that accept on-prem ranges.
alex: ran `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=attachment.instance-owner-id,Values=vpce-* --query '[].{Id:NetworkInterfaceId,Groups:Groups}'` — vpce ENIs present and SG is the restrictive one.
ryan: temp fix — updated VPCE SG to allow 172.30.0.0/16 (on-prem proxy nat range). After rule add, ecr pulls and artifact downloads resumed.
lisa: confirmed. Workaround works. Root cause appears to be: egress path -> TGW -> on-prem proxy rewrites source, return traffic comes back via TGW and hits the VPCE ENI SG which rejects it because SG expects native VPC source.
tam: follow-up items: 1) automation to sync endpoint SGs with on-prem egress ranges OR 2) route endpoint subnets to return directly (avoid hairpin through proxy) OR 3) use a different pattern (NLB-backed endpoint service on our side so proxy doesn't rewrite).
maria: also note private DNS / split-horizon could mask this in other clusters — add a check in our endpoint hardening runbook: verify SGs include TGW/onprem ranges when TGW routes exist.
alex: I'll open INFRA-1429 to add SG sync + runbook and bump priority. Thanks for quick triage everyone :thumbsup:
lisa: long-term: audit all interface endpoints in peered/TGW-connected VPCs. We should also document that VPCE ENIs can be sensitive to asymmetric routing and proxy translation.
ops-bot: ticket INFRA-1429 created by alex (priority: P2).
alex: closing the loop — rolling restart looks green and fails stopped after SG change. Will keep ticket for automation. Thanks! :white_check_mark:
